routes.label: Consider the role of the 70-degree angle

question: Two angles of an isosceles triangle measure \(70^\circ\) and \(x^\circ.\) What is the sum of the three possible values of \(x?\)
solution:
An isosceles triangle has two equal base angles, and its three angles sum to \(180^\circ\). The given \(70^\circ\) angle can be either a base angle or the vertex angle.

If it is a base angle, the other base angle is also \(70^\circ\), and the vertex angle is
\[
180^\circ-70^\circ-70^\circ=40^\circ.
\]
The angle labeled \(x^\circ\) can therefore be either \(70^\circ\) or \(40^\circ\).

If \(70^\circ\) is the vertex angle, the equal base angles each measure
\[
\frac{180^\circ-70^\circ}{2}=55^\circ,
\]
so \(x=55\).

These two cases exhaust the roles of the given angle and produce three distinct possible values. Their sum is
\[
70+40+55=\boxed{165},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
